title: Security advisory: Critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, update now
locator: 21 October security advisory: opening; Who is at risk; How to update; incomplete mitigations
appraisal: Maintainer operational advisory inspected directly. Establishes release-specific fixes and vendor-update route, not prevalence or current exploitation. Recheck before operations; do not generalize temporary settings.

title: Today's PHP Security Release, and How We're Strengthening PHP Security
locator: A first external audit and increased security focus; Building a sustainable professional security organization
appraisal: First-party account of audit, early 2024 signs, stalled fixes, subsequent reports and human patch decisions. Fundraising interests disclosed in source. Shares incident origin with S1; not independent replication.

title: Critical Security Vulnerability in React Server Components
locator: Opening disclosure/date; Immediate Action Required: unaffected applications; Affected frameworks and bundlers including next
appraisal: Maintainer disclosure; inspected affected package and unaffected deployment qualifications. Updated January 26, 2026. Historical comparison only, no current React version instructions or AI discovery attribution adopted.

title: Partnering with Mozilla to improve Firefox’s security
locator: Opening: 22 findings over two weeks; From identifying vulnerabilities to writing primitive exploits: two cases, several hundred trials, reduced protections
appraisal: Vendor report with commercial interest, not controlled human/AI comparison. Mozilla advisory corroborates attribution/severity but not independently the entire count, duration or exploit evaluation. Test environment excluded normal sandbox protections.

title: Security Vulnerabilities fixed in Firefox 148
locator: CVE-2026-2763 and CVE-2026-2764: reporter and high impact; other Claude-credited entries
appraisal: Maintainer confirmation of individual fixes, reporters using Claude and severity. Same collaboration origin as S4; not an independent experiment.

title: Joint statement on critical PHP vulnerabilities
locator: Identify PHP-based applications; coordinate with providers; prioritize internet-facing systems; isolation; third-party products with embedded PHP
appraisal: Official operational recommendations for this incident. Normative guidance, not measured efficacy of a general security intervention. CVE information derives from PHP disclosure.

title: Docker Security Cheat Sheet
appraisal: Practitioner hardening guidance specific to Docker. Recommendations are not an empirical guarantee against unknown vulnerabilities. Only the relevant control passages were inspected; no deployment was audited.

title: Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1
locator: PO.2.1 printed p. 6/PDF p. 15; PW.8.2 printed p. 15/PDF p. 24; RV.2 printed pp. 17–18/PDF pp. 26–27
appraisal: Original NIST guidance inspected in relevant table passages. Used for responsibilities, documented testing and planned responses, not effectiveness data or an assertion this is the newest SSDF edition. No risk calculation or notional scenario adopted.

title: Assessing Claude Mythos Preview’s cybersecurity capabilities
locator: Introduction/date; The significance of Claude Mythos Preview: overnight RCE cases and limited partner release; Suggestions for defenders: no general availability
appraisal: Vendor capability report. Relevant passages inspected directly; examples are attributed and do not yield a representative discovery rate, controlled human speed comparison or Node.js attribution. Later model; March Opus results cannot be treated as a ceiling.

title: Redeploying Fable 5
locator: July 1 update: restored access; opening: June 12 suspension, June 30 lifting of controls, initially restored Mythos access for a set of US organizations; Timeline: June 9 release
appraisal: First-party historical account, updated July 1. Records vendor explanation of compliance and restoration, not an independent legal finding or current access guarantee. Distinguish Mythos Preview restrictions from Mythos 5/Fable 5 suspension.

title: Wednesday, October 21, 2026 Security Releases
locator: Security releases available; CVE-2026-111497 Brotli decoder section
appraisal: Original project advisory inspected. Supports released updates, affected release lines and high-severity RCE issue. Does not establish AI discovery, exploitation in the wild, or faster future CVE discovery.

title: NVD CVE API 2.0 — publication-window count snapshots
locator: figures/raw/month-01.json through month-10.json and day-01.json through day-21.json: totalResults, timestamp; companion -request.json files contain exact queries and SHA-256
appraisal: Original API responses directly retrieved and inspected. Count by published UTC date with noRejected, not CVE ID year. All October daily windows reconcile to monthly count. Live database may change; cumulative sums are arithmetic transformations, not modelled estimates. No inference about discovery speed, attacks or AI attribution. HTML API documentation fetch returned 403; not represented as inspected.

title: Django security releases issued: 6.1.2, 6.0.9, and 5.2.18
locator: CVE-2026-84429: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in HTTP header parsing; severity paragraph; Affected supported versions and Resolution
appraisal: Original maintainer disclosure directly inspected. Supports affected parser, unauthenticated header reachability and moderate severity according to Django policy. No AI discovery attribution or assertion every Django deployment is exposed. Other issues in the release not counted or pooled.

title: Spring Security DPoPProofJwtDecoderFactory vulnerable to DPoP Proof Replay
locator: Heading: HIGH/August 20/CVE; Description; Affected Spring Products and Versions; Mitigation
appraisal: Original project advisory directly inspected. Component-specific conditional vulnerability, not all Spring applications. Attack requires intercepted valid proof and cache eviction. No exploit testing, AI attribution or current version recommendation adopted.
